problem: Ayumi carried 6 seashells in her small bucket. Her uncle filled his big pail with 4 times as many. How many seashells are in the pail?
How many apples did the farmer pack in the crate, if Teo's lunch bag held 6 apples and the crate held 4 times as many?

The Garcia orchard picked 72 baskets of plums this summer, 8 times as many as the small orchard down the road. The road between them is 20 kilometres long. How many baskets did the small orchard pick?
follow_up_questions: The small orchard sells each basket for 7 dollars. How much money does it make if it sells them all?
How many baskets did the two orchards pick altogether?

problem: How many trophies does the junior team have, if the senior team's 72 trophies are 8 times as many and the club was founded 50 years ago?
follow_up_questions: Each junior trophy cost 7 dollars to engrave. What did the engraving cost?
How many trophies do the two teams have in total?

problem: Ollie bought 2 kites at the beach shop. His cousins, who wanted to fly them as a big group, bought 10. How many times as many kites did the cousins buy?
follow_up_questions: The cousins paint stripes on 3 of their kites. How many kites have no stripes?

problem: How many times as many cupcakes did Mrs Novak bake as Jun, if Jun baked 2 and Mrs Novak baked 10 for the school party?
follow_up_questions: Mrs Novak puts sprinkles on 3 of her cupcakes. How many of hers have no sprinkles?

problem: A school garden has 26 bricks around the herb bed. The new pond needs 4 times as many bricks for its edge. A frog statue sits beside the pond. How many bricks does the pond's edge need?
follow_up_questions: A wheelbarrow carries 8 bricks on each trip. How many trips does it take to bring the pond's bricks?

problem: How many chairs did the hall set out for the evening concert, if 26 were set out for the morning practice and the concert needed 4 times as many? The piano had just been tuned.
follow_up_questions: A trolley moves 8 chairs at a time. How many trolley trips did the concert chairs take?

problem: At the market, Mr Osei bought 18 small oranges. Melons were heavy, so he bought only a third as many melons. How many melons did he buy?
follow_up_questions: At home, each melon was cut into 4 slices. How many slices were there?
Two of the slices fell on the floor. How many slices were left?
The good slices were shared equally between his two children. How many slices did each child get?

problem: How many large posters did a teacher buy for the classroom, if she bought 18 postcards and a third as many posters?
follow_up_questions: She cuts each poster into 4 parts for a collage. How many parts are there?
Two parts get torn and are thrown out. How many parts are still good?
The good parts are split equally between two groups of pupils. How many parts does each group get?

problem: Ines's sunflower grew 9 centimetres in a month. The tallest sunflower in the contest grew 72 centimetres, far more than hers. How many times as much as Ines's sunflower did the tallest one grow?
follow_up_questions: Next month Ines hopes her sunflower grows twice as much as this month. How much growth is she hoping for?
Even then, how many centimetres less than the tallest sunflower's growth would that be?

problem: How many times as heavy as Kenji's watermelon is the prize watermelon, which weighs 72 kilograms, far more than Kenji's 9 kilograms?
follow_up_questions: Kenji wants next year's melon to weigh twice as much as this one. What weight is that?
How many kilograms lighter than this year's prize melon would that still be?

problem: Sofia folded 5 paper cranes, and her grandmother, who folds very fast, made double that number. How many cranes did her grandmother fold?
How many laps did Amir run, if he ran double the 5 laps his little sister ran?
A garden show had 14 rose bushes on display. Tulips are the town's favourite, so there were 6 times as many tulip pots. How many tulip pots were there?
follow_up_questions: Each helper watered 7 tulip pots, and each pot had only one helper. How many helpers were there?
A quarter of the tulip pots won prizes. How many pots won prizes?
How many tulip pots won no prize?

problem: How many paintings hung in the art show, if there were 14 sculptures and 6 times as many paintings?
follow_up_questions: Each visitor group looked closely at 7 paintings, and every painting was seen by just one group. How many groups were there?
A quarter of the paintings were sold. How many paintings were sold?
How many paintings were not sold?

problem: A piggy bank held 80 coins. Mia guessed only half that number. Her dog was barking at the door. What was Mia's guess?
follow_up_questions: Her brother guessed 10 more than Mia. What was his guess?

problem: What was Raj's guess, if the fish tank had 80 pebbles and he guessed half the real number? The tank had a bubbling filter.
follow_up_questions: His friend guessed 10 more than Raj did. What was her guess?

problem: At the farm, a cow drinks 96 litres of water a day and a goat drinks 8 litres. How many times as much does the cow drink?
How many times as long as an 8-metre rowing boat is a 96-metre ship in the harbour?
Mei caught 7 fish at the lake. That was only half as many as her uncle caught. How many fish did her uncle catch?
follow_up_questions: They put all their fish in one bucket. How many fish are in the bucket?
They cook 15 of the fish for dinner. How many fish are left?

problem: How many stickers did Pablo earn this week if Sara earned 7, only half as many as Pablo?
follow_up_questions: They put their stickers together on one chart. How many stickers are on the chart?
They swap 15 stickers for a toy. How many stickers do they have left?

problem: A school canteen served 63 bowls of soup on Monday, 7 times as many as the salads the salad bar served. Lunch began at 12. How many salads were served?
follow_up_questions: Each salad costs 5 dollars. How much money did the salad bar take?

problem: How many boat trips did the lake give on Sunday, if the park train gave 63 trips, 7 times as many, and the park closed at 6?
follow_up_questions: A boat trip costs 5 tokens. How many tokens did the boats collect?

problem: In the pet shop window there are 5 rabbits and 30 guinea pigs. How many times as many guinea pigs as rabbits are there?
follow_up_questions: The shop gets 6 more guinea pigs. How many guinea pigs are there now?
The guinea pigs are then put into 4 cages with the same number in each. How many go in each cage?

problem: Find how many times as many ducklings as geese there are at the pond, where 5 geese swim beside 30 ducklings.
follow_up_questions: Another 6 ducklings hatch. How many ducklings are there now?
The ducklings are split into 4 equal groups for a photo. How many are in each group?

problem: Lucy's paper plane flew 18 metres. Her teacher's plane flew 6 times as far. How far did the teacher's plane fly?
What length of string does the big kite fly on, if the small kite flies on an 18-metre string and the big one on a string 6 times as long?
At the spelling bee, the red team spelled 36 words correctly. The yellow team got only a quarter as many right. The hall had just been painted. How many words did the yellow team spell correctly?
follow_up_questions: In a bonus round, the yellow team spells 15 more words correctly. What is its total now?

problem: How many goals did the second team score this season, if the first team scored 36 and the second scored only a quarter as many? The pitch was muddy all winter.
follow_up_questions: In the summer cup, the second team adds 15 more goals. What is its total now?

problem: Mr Hale's table had 8 paintbrushes for the art lesson, while the other tables had 88 altogether. The other tables had how many times as many brushes?
follow_up_questions: The other tables' brushes are put into 4 jars, the same number in each. How many brushes are in each jar?
Mr Hale's table puts its brushes into one of the jars. How many are in that jar now?
Later, 9 brushes from that jar are left to soak in the sink. How many are still in the jar?

problem: How many times as many marbles do the older children have as Kim, if Kim has 8 and the older children have 88 altogether?
follow_up_questions: The older children share their marbles equally into 4 bags. How many marbles go in each bag?
Kim pours her marbles into one of the bags. How many marbles are in that bag now?
Then 9 marbles roll out of that bag under the sofa. How many are left in the bag?

problem: Kemal can hold his breath underwater for 9 seconds. His swimming teacher can hold hers 8 times as long. How long can the teacher hold her breath?
follow_up_questions: After a month of practice, Kemal can hold his breath 4 times as long as before. How long is that?
How many more seconds does Kemal need to match his teacher?

problem: What was the number of hula-hoop spins Coach Alvarez managed, if Sasha's best was 9 spins and the coach managed 8 times as many?
follow_up_questions: After practising, Sasha's best becomes 4 times her old one. What is her new best?
How many more spins does Sasha need to equal the coach?

problem: In the reading challenge, the top class read 84 books. The bottom class read a quarter as many. Each child got a bookmark from a pack of 50. How many books did the bottom class read?
follow_up_questions: Each book the bottom class read raised 3 pounds for the library. How much money did they raise?

problem: How many kilometres did Dad cycle on Saturday, if Mum cycled 84 kilometres on Sunday and Dad cycled a quarter as far? They stopped for lunch at a cafe with 12 tables.
follow_up_questions: Dad raised 3 pounds for charity for each kilometre he cycled. How much did he raise?

problem: Fatima's snail crawled 20 centimetres before stopping. Her brother's snail stopped after 5 centimetres. How many times as far as her brother's snail did Fatima's snail crawl?
How many times as long as a 5-minute song is a 20-minute cartoon?
For the school fair, the pupils baked 26 cakes, and the parents baked 7 times as many cookies. The fair opens at 10 in the morning. How many cookies did the parents bake?
follow_up_questions: The cookies are shared equally among 14 stalls. How many cookies does each stall get?
One stall drops 4 of its cookies. How many does that stall still have?

problem: How many seeds did the gardening club plant, if it planted 7 times as many seeds as the 26 bulbs it planted, and the club has 9 members?
follow_up_questions: The seeds were planted equally in 14 rows. How many seeds are in each row?
Birds eat 4 seeds from one row. How many seeds are left in that row?

problem: The snack table gave out 45 bananas on picnic day. The apples ran out early, so only a third as many apples were given out. How many apples were given out?
follow_up_questions: How many pieces of fruit were given out altogether?

problem: How many paper plates were used at the party, if 45 paper cups were used and a third as many plates?
follow_up_questions: All the cups and plates went in the recycling bin afterwards. How many items were recycled?
